name: Perineum Discovery
text: Begin with comfortable external contact around the area between your genitals and anus. Choose still contact, light touch or no direct contact at all. Notice the sensation without expecting it to become arousing.
safetyNote: Avoid pressure on wounds, irritated skin, or recent surgical sites.

name: Pressure & Release
text: Explore external touch at a comfortable intensity. Try maintaining gentle contact, then releasing it completely. Notice whether the change affects your sensation. Do not increase pressure simply because you are not feeling a strong response.
safetyNote: Avoid forceful pressure. The aim is exploration, not compression of underlying structures.

name: Breath & Sensation
text: Let your breathing remain comfortable. If you wish, breathe in gently for 4 seconds and out for 6 seconds. Notice how your body feels during contact and during pauses. Breathing supports awareness and relaxation, but cannot guarantee a particular arousal response.
safetyNote: Do not require breath holding. If dizziness occurs, stop and return to natural breathing.

name: Prostate-Area Exploration (External)
text: This optional card is for people who know they have a prostate and want to explore external sensations around the perineum. Use comfortable contact only — external pressure does not guarantee direct prostate stimulation. If you don't have a prostate or don't want prostate-specific guidance, use the general Perineum Discovery card instead.
safetyNote: The external perineum card is available to everyone. Only the prostate-specific description is anatomy-dependent.

name: Prostate Exploration (Internal)
text: This optional card is for people with a prostate who actively want to explore internal stimulation. Internal contact is NOT required for pleasure. You can choose external contact, relaxation, or no stimulation instead. If choosing internal contact: use adequate lubricant, clean hands, and a toy with a flared base. Stop immediately if there is pain, bleeding, or increasing discomfort.
safetyNote: This card links to a dedicated safety screen before users enter internal-exploration mode. Do not use a timer countdown to encourage tolerating discomfort.
